answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Tracing. Each identity carries a compact summary of its action patterns from prior epochs; on re-entry, the summary must match newly observed behaviour within a set tolerance. A fable spread across fresh keys breaks this because summaries don't transfer — each new key starts blank and must slowly rebuild history. Attackers thus pay a replay cost: every sybil must wander through many epochs of genuine-looking activity before matching its own fabricated record.
